subject_area: Object-oriented Java programming — applied APIs and GUI
pedagogical_level: undergraduate fundamentals course with hands-on Java coding
course_intent: Build on introductory OOP by teaching students to write working Java applications that use exception handling, Swing GUIs, file I/O and serialization, JDBC database access, and basic multithreading — students should leave able to implement small Java desktop applications that integrate these standard library APIs.
depth_bound: Recommendations stay at the level of standard-library Java API usage and small application-level code. JVM internals, advanced concurrency theory (memory models, lock-free algorithms), modern GUI frameworks (JavaFX/web), ORM frameworks (Hibernate/JPA depth), enterprise frameworks (Spring), and build/deployment tooling are beyond this course's depth.
key_topics: Inheritance, polymorphism, method overriding/overloading with Employee hierarchy
try/catch/finally exception handling and custom exception types
Swing GUI components (JFrame, JButton, JTextArea, JTable, layout managers)
Sequential text file I/O with Formatter and Scanner
NIO Path/Paths/Files for file and directory information
JDBC: Connection, Statement, ResultSet, PreparedStatement, RowSet
SQL fundamentals (SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, INNER JOIN, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE)
Thread life cycle and states; Runnable interface and ExecutorService
one_liner: Second-semester Java OOP course teaching applied use of standard Java APIs — exception handling, Swing GUIs, file/serialization I/O, JDBC with SQL, and basic threading via Executors — at hands-on code level, but does NOT cover modern frameworks (Spring, JavaFX, Hibernate), advanced concurrency theory, or build/deployment tooling.
